clue.text: Duke bad rings turned into ornament

indicators.note: turned says the words bad and rings are read together backwards

parts.note: a printing slip for had, taken as written
rings are round shapes, two letter Os

explanation.surface: A duke has some bad rings made into a decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'bad', a slip for 'had'; 'turned' reverses the two pieces together as one run, which then follows the duke.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is a colloquial word for a trinket or knick-knack, an ornamental thing.

clue.text: Move quickly to get on target for guided missiles

parts.note: to dart is to move quickly
to board a vehicle is to get on it

explanation.surface: Rushing to get a guided missile on target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guided missiles' suggests weaponry; it means darts aimed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts are thrown missiles aimed at a circular board.

clue.text: Block giving Doc clue to disorder

indicators.note: to disorder says the letters of Doc and clue are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's hint about an illness that blocks things.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to obstruct or close off, as an artery.

clue.text: Follow Nanny's example? Hardly!

parts.note: a nanny goat behaving like itself is literally playing the goat; 'Hardly!' says it is foolish, not sensible

explanation.surface: A child refusing to copy the sensible nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanny is a female goat, not a childminder.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool about or behave in a silly way.

clue.text: Daily record of passing interest

parts.note: a daily newspaper's account of someone who has passed away, read as a record of 'passing interest'

explanation.surface: A newspaper's diary of things only mildly interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing interest' suggests something trivial, but 'passing' means dying: this is the newspaper column about the recently dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper notice recording a death and the life of the deceased is printed daily.

clue.text: Outstretched leg, perhaps, in attack

parts.note: broad means wide, stretched out
in cricket the leg side is one side of the field

explanation.surface: Someone attacks with a leg stretched out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the leg side, so leg is an example of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal attack, originally a ship's full volley.

clue.text: Excessively sentimental material needs cutting

indicators.note: needs cutting says the material word loses its last letter

parts.note: tweed is a woollen material

explanation.surface: Fabric overly sentimental needs trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means affectedly quaint or cute, overly sweet.

clue.text: One without a place to get item published

parts.note: item in Latin means likewise, also
a paper ran a story when it published it

explanation.surface: A writer without a position gets an item into print.
explanation.walkthrough: Item, from Latin, introduces a further point in a list, meaning also.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that finishes unplaced.

clue.text: You investigate every little detail — leads to turn over

indicators.note: leads points to the first letters of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Investigating every last detail leads to a surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender, to hand something over.

clue.text: Not a sign of times, unless you change the angle

definitions.text: Not a sign of times, unless you change the angle

parts.words: Not a sign of times, unless you change the angle
parts.note: the multiplication sign turned through forty-five degrees becomes the addition sign

explanation.surface: Something no longer typical of the age unless viewed differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign of times' suggests 'sign of the times' but means the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The addition symbol is a cross upright, the times sign tilted.

clue.text: Claret I put out for the performance

indicators.note: put out suggests the claret and I letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a bottle of claret before going to a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Some in Dover seem to manage

indicators.note: Some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people in the port of Dover appear able to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, which is to manage something.

clue.text: Ignore a team after confrontation

indicators.note: after places the words a team behind the confrontation word

parts.note: a brush is a brief hostile encounter, as in a brush with the law
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A team is snubbed following a clash.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush aside something is to dismiss or disregard it.

clue.text: Source of power king and I had

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A king and I possessed a power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is George Rex, a king's royal cipher seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Grid is the network supplying electrical power across Britain.

clue.text: For example, Jonathan — with brass accompaniment, of course

parts.note: Jonathan is a variety of eating fruit from an orchard tree
brass and sauce both mean cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A man named Jonathan plays alongside a brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan looks like a name; it is an American apple variety. 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple sauce is served alongside a dish, traditionally pork, in one course of a meal.

clue.text: One who indulges in something sweet

definitions.text: One who indulges in something sweet

parts.words: One who indulges in something sweet
parts.note: revenge is said to be sweet, so one who takes it indulges in something sweet

explanation.surface: Someone with a sweet tooth treating themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cakes; the proverb 'revenge is sweet' gives the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes vengeance enjoys revenge, proverbially sweet.

clue.text: Came back with circular about editor

indicators.note: about says the circular word goes around the editor abbreviation

parts.note: rounded means circular in shape

explanation.surface: An editor returned with a circular.
explanation.definitionFit: To redound is to rebound or recoil, to come back on someone.

clue.text: One politician elected, for example, returned to make an impact

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament
a candidate elected is in

indicators.note: returned says the abbreviation for for example is read backwards

explanation.surface: A newly elected MP comes back wanting to make a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge is to have an effect on something, to strike against it.

clue.text: Spirit shown by English, with the French in mind

parts.note: le is French for the
mental means relating to the mind

explanation.surface: An English person's spirit with French culture in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a nature spirit, one of the beings of earth, air, fire or water.

clue.text: Reject out of hand

parts.note: in card games, a card thrown away from the hand is rejected out of it

explanation.surface: Refusing something immediately without consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hand' means summarily, but here it is literal: a card taken out of a player's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw away an unwanted card from a hand in a card game; also to reject generally.

clue.text: Cross sailor getting over anger

indicators.note: getting over places the sailor word above the anger word in this down light

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
ire means anger

explanation.surface: An irritable sailor gets over losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is an X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Blow up revolutionary general

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the word general is overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel general blows something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Fencing, encounter trouble in fighting area

indicators.note: in says the trouble word sits inside the fighting area word

parts.note: a boxing ring is a fighting area
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Fencers run into trouble in the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests swordplay; it means railings round a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing is a fence of rails, a barrier.

clue.text: Outstanding example of clue endlessly being copied

indicators.note: being copied says the remaining letters appear twice over
endlessly says the word clue loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A model clue that keeps getting imitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is slang for a remarkable person or thing, a humdinger.

clue.text: Pound German got in game of chance

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra
Otto is a common German name

explanation.surface: A German brings money into a gambling game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of drawing numbers by chance, like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Good results I have, one after another

parts.note: success means a good result or results
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a string of good results.
explanation.definitionFit: Successive things follow in sequence, consecutively.

clue.text: Nice people might scoff at one

definitions.text: Nice people might scoff at one

parts.words: Nice people might scoff at one
parts.note: residents of Nice in France might eat at a French coffee house

explanation.surface: Polite people might sneer at something.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective; scoff means eat, not mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small restaurant where people eat and drink.

clue.text: Part of tree left something to be desired?

definitions.text: Part of tree left something to be desired?

parts.words: Part of tree left something to be desired?
parts.note: a member of a family tree who is left something in a will, a successor to be wished for

explanation.surface: A tree that disappointed somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left something to be desired' means fell short; here it is literal: someone bequeathed something, and a wanted successor.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is a family member who inherits property.

clue.text: The last place where you'd expect to find Charlie

definitions.text: The last place where you'd expect to find Charlie

parts.words: The last place where you'd expect to find Charlie
parts.note: '... Charlie' is the name for the last in a line, so the rear is exactly where Charlie is found

explanation.surface: Somewhere Charlie would never be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last place you'd expect' usually means unlikely; here 'last' is literal, from 'tail-end Charlie', the rear gunner or last in a convoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear end or final part of something, the last position.

clue.text: Beastly authority quickly introducing university cut

indicators.note: introducing says the shortened university word is put into the word for quickly

parts.note: fast means quickly
uni is the cut-down form of university

explanation.surface: An expert rushes in with a cut to university funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A faunist is an expert on animal life, an authority on beasts.

clue.text: Cancel deliveries before journey

indicators.note: before puts the deliveries word ahead of the journey word

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone cancels deliveries before setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled, each a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to annul or set it aside.

clue.text: Boy and girl in old part of India

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is a colloquial word for girl

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl in a historical region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India, now split between India and Bangladesh.
